title: Data and Code
text:
BioGeoSyn
An R package that wraps BioGeoBEARS in a step-by-step graphical interface, so that ancestral-range reconstruction and model comparison become reproducible — and comparable across clades.



Reproducible GUI


A five-step wizard from data upload to results, with standardised output tables and publication-ready figures.




Cross-clade synthesis


Pools biogeographic event statistics across multiple groups: range expansion, speciation modes, vicariance and extinction.




Guarded state space


Automated state-space monitoring and performance optimisation, so analyses fail fast instead of running for days.




Advanced constraints


Time stratification, dispersal multipliers and area-adjacency matrices, all configurable from the interface.




Reports


HTML and PDF report generation directly from a completed run.




Portable bundles


Result bundles that can be shared with collaborators or attached to a manuscript.




Install
remotes::install_github("XuWeiEvo/BioGeoSyn")
BioGeoBEARS must be installed separately; the app ships with an environment checker that helps with setup.


Run
library(BioGeoSyn)
launch_app()          # interactive GUI
# or, scripted:
run_workflow()

GitHub repository Preprint (bioRxiv)

title: Wei Xu徐伟
text:
Macroevolution · Macroecology · Conservation


Wei Xu徐伟


Postdoctoral researcher, Tel Aviv University, Israel


I study how Earth history, climate and traits build the biodiversity we see today — from Himalayan amphibians to Malagasy rainforest trees — and how that knowledge becomes conservation on the ground.

What I work on




Mountains as diversity engines


How uplift and climate history shaped the Himalaya, the Qinghai–Tibetan Plateau and the Hengduan Mountains — and why different vertebrate groups answered the same geology in different ways.




Large-scale conservation


Translating macroecological and phylogenetic evidence into conservation priorities at national and continental scale — as in our PNAS study revealing the hidden hotspots of amphibian biodiversity in China.




Trait diversity and evolution


How functional traits originate, diversify and drive radiations: frugivory-related traits across the global Annonaceae of tropical rainforests, and the trait innovations behind the worldwide radiation of modern toads.




Theory


Developing the conceptual side of macroevolution and macroecology — the theory that the tools should rest on. Work in progress; nothing published yet.




Software development


Building open tools for macroevolution and macroecology, starting with BioGeoSyn — making biogeographic inference reproducible and comparable across clades — with more to come.
